newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Third Cambodian oil and gas venture comes up dry.
newsitem.headline: Third Cambodian oil and gas venture comes up dry.

text.p: Britain's Premier Oil and its Australian partner are ending their oil and gas exploration programme in Cambodia, a Premier official said on Tuesday.
They are withdrawing from a partnership that has spent $23 million off the country's coast, Premier manager for Cambodia Jeremy Martin said.
Martin said one of Premier's partners, Japan's Idemitsu Cambodia Oil Exploration Co Ltd, would continue exploration, but the third partner in the venture, Australia's Ampolex Ltd, would not.
The partners, which each have 33.3 percent stakes in the venture, would transfer all operations to Idemitsu, he said.
Martin told Reuters the firms were withdrawing because the results of recent seismic surveys had been disappointing. But Idemitsu was "more optimistic than we are", he added.

The announcement comes after the only other partnerships exploring for oil off Cambodia's coast, those led by Britain's Enterprise Oil and Cambodia Petroleum Exploration Co Ltd (Campex), said in December that they had also come up dry.

Impoverished Cambodia had hoped for rich oil and gas finds off its coast but must now turn its sights on to the Overlapping Claim Area (OCA), a section of the Gulf of Thailand claimed by both Cambodia and Thailand.
Cambodia is reviewing bids for the OCA, after which it is expected to enter negotiations with Thailand, which awarded concessions in the OCA in the 1970s.
Analysts expect it could take years before the countries reach agreement and companies can begin exploring the area.
The three ventures that have explored the area closer to Cambodia told Reuters their results were disappointing.

Martin said Premier, Ampolex and Idemitsu were awarded rights to explore Block IV offshore in 1991,and drilled one well in 1994. The Koh Tang-1 well yielded some hydrocarbons with a maximum daily flow rate of 1,180 barrels of oil and 1.3 million cubic feet of gas, according to the Ministry of Commerce.
Martin said that the well was not commercially viable, adding: "Basically, yes, we are through in Cambodia."
Enterprise's $55 million exploration programme at four wells has also yielded no commercially viable oil or gas discoveries, though the firm is still optimistic about the OCA.
Campex, a subsidiary of the Japan Petroleum Exploration Co Ltd (Japex), has found no commercial wells after drilling at two sites offshore.
